chunks: Al-Fayz ibn al-Mukhtar gifted a sea bass to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and brought it to him, and I was with him. So he looked at it and said: 'This has scales on it,' so he ate from it, and we were watching him.

key_terms.أَهْدَى: He gifted or presented as a gift.
key_terms.رَبِيثَا: A type of fish, specifically sea bass or a similar saltwater fish, known for having scales.
key_terms.قِشْرٌ: Scales (of a fish), indicating the feature that makes it permissible to eat according to Shia jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about the scales of the fish when it was gifted to him?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s direct engagement with daily sustenance, using the sea bass (rabita) to demonstrate the permissibility of fish with scales. The detail of the Imam eating it in the presence of his companion serves as a practical legal proof (hujjah) for the Shias regarding the consumption of this specific type of fish, reinforcing the principle of permissibility unless explicitly prohibited.

en.hubeali: ‘Al-Fayz Bin Mukhtar gifted sea bass to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, and I was in his<sup>asws</sup> presence. So he<sup>asws</sup> looked at it and said: ‘This has scales on it, therefore eat from it’, and we saw him<sup>asws</sup> (eating it)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Hanan ibn Sadir has the following: “

Once, al-Fayd ibn al-Mukhtar sent rabitha as gift to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. It was brought for him when I was present. He (the Imam) looked at it and said, ‘This has scales.’ He (the Imam) ate thereof and we saw him eating.”’
